doc.title: Eddie Palmieri — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Moving to the Bronx and his prodigy brother Charlie
summary: He left El Barrio at 5 or 6; brother Charlie, nine years older, was already a prodigy playing in bands.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So you were born in el barrio, but you moved to South Bronx at what age? Do you remember?
Oh, no more than 5 or 6. So I don’t remember much about el barrio. My brother was 14, and already playing piano. He was a genius, a prodigy, Charlie.

The only problem that my brother had was he was already playing with some of the bands that, “Oh, the prodigy, the Palmieri kid, Charlie Palmieri,” and everything went fine, except at the end of the gig they would tell him, “Charlie, your mother’s waiting for you outside.” That didn’t go over too well. His mother!? My mother was very stern and took care of us. Because of her we became musicians.
